status_summary: No proposed or final OCR rule since 2025-01-20 on crisis standards of care, quality-adjusted life years or denial of treatment to disabled newborns was found. As context only, HHS published a proposed rule on 2025-12-19 that would amend only the Section 504 exclusions provision on gender dysphoria, leaving the 2024 Section 504 rule's other provisions in place, and a final rule adopting it with unchanged text (FR Doc. 2026-22380, RIN 0945-AA27) was scheduled for publication on 2026-11-03, effective 60 days after publication per its public inspection copy; neither addresses the three subjects. H.R. 3864, introduced 2025-06-10 and still in committee, would bar federal health programs from using quality-adjusted life years in coverage and payment decisions by statute; it is not the OCR rulemaking the recommendation describes.

timeline.event: H.R. 3864, the Protecting Health Care for All Patients Act of 2025, was introduced in the House and referred to the Ways and Means and Energy and Commerce Committees; it would amend Social Security Act section 1182(e) to bar federal health programs from using quality-adjusted life years in coverage and payment decisions. No later action is recorded; it is related legislation, not an OCR rule.

title: Issue disability rules on crisis standards of care, QALYs and denial of care to newborns
uncertainties: No proposed or final OCR rule since 2025-01-20 on crisis standards of care, quality-adjusted life years or denial of treatment to disabled newborns was found. The HHS Unified Agenda rule list on reginfo.gov (Agency Rule List - 2026) lists OCR Section 504 entries on the gender dysphoria exclusion and web accessibility deadlines and a Section 1557 revision, none on these subjects. The 2024 Section 504 rule reportedly contains overlapping value assessment provisions; it predates the period and its text was not opened. H.R. 3864 would bar QALY use by statute and remains in committee. The Trump-era drafts and the older newborn rule were not located. The absence checks were last run systematically on 2026-10-19. The 2026-11-03 HHS final rule on the Section 504 gender dysphoria exclusion (FR Doc. 2026-22380, RIN 0945-AA27, 45 CFR part 84) was read in its public inspection copy on public-inspection.federalregister.gov through about 100,000 of 121,900 characters; it adopts the 2025-12-19 proposal unchanged, is effective 60 days after publication (about 2027-01-02, an inference), and in the part read contains no provision on crisis standards of care, quality-adjusted life years, newborn treatment or assisted suicide. Its Federal Register API record could not be opened on federalregister.gov in this review, so the 91 FR citation and signer were not confirmed. Because the proposal and the final rule concern a different Section 504 subject, they are kept as context in sources and status_summary and are not timeline events for this record.
